title: Bitcoin's $64,000 slide

lines: gone from the price of a single Bitcoin since its October 2025 peak.
Bitcoin traded near $61,600 on Nov. 19 — down about 13% in a week, closing in on $60,000.
The price is now roughly half that — a sixth straight losing week. (Crypto Briefing)
Own a Bitcoin ETF in your brokerage or 401(k)? Then you own this drop.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs have shed over $2.5 billion in 2026, per CoinDesk.
The same door that let crypto into retirement accounts lets a near-50% drop in too.

source_line: Sources: The Motley Fool (Nov 19), Crypto Briefing, 2026
caption:
About $64,000 has come off the price of a single Bitcoin since its October 2025 peak near $126,000 — it traded around $61,600 on Nov. 19, closing in on $60,000 (The Motley Fool, Crypto Briefing).

That's roughly half its all-time high, and a sixth straight losing week. The twist: Bitcoin now lives inside brokerage accounts and some 401(k)s through spot ETFs — which have shed more than $2.5 billion in 2026, per CoinDesk, as the Fed signals higher rates for longer.

My take: the same door that let crypto into retirement accounts lets a near-50% drawdown in too.
